yes. I always wondered why it sometimes gives some search results. appears it mostly happened because the author name had that word in it.

It makes no sence to search for author name in the World search by default in my opinion. Of course it should be an option, but not the default. Or at least the weighting should be way less than it currently is, so worlds where searchword parts are included in the author name appear way later in the list.

details:
Currently, the world search returns a lot of unrelevant results.

Example of a World:

- World title: ABC

- World description: Chill, solve puzzles or play the escape room.

- Tags: escape room puzzles

- Creator: XYZ

If a user searches for "escape room", the world above will not appear in the search results. Why not? It seems, that the standard search does only search in the title and for the autor name. The search will find any world which has "escape" OR "room" in the title (or in the author name). But this returns results, that are far away, from what the user is looking for. 

If a creator wants to be found by "escape room", he currently must add the keywords in the title. But this is not always desirable, because it causes long and ugly titles.

I know, there is a extendend/custom search. But I don't think, this will be used by main users, because it's well hidden. Also several clicks are needed to find "escape room" within tags.

Suggestion:

The default world search should additionally search in description and in tags, because these are more relevant than the title. Also, the search should be AND by default. If a user searches for "escape room", he doesn't wan't find a world, which is a "movie room" for example.

Also, if a user searches for "puzzle" and the creator has defined "puzzles" in the tags, the world should be listed in the results. Joined tags like "escaperoom" or "escape_room" should also be considered in the results.
title: World search currently useless
